topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under 12-10-218(1)(a), what two elements must BOTH be present for an arrangement to qualify as an "affiliated business arrangement"?
choice_a: An affiliate relationship or a direct beneficial ownership interest of more than one percent in another settlement service provider, AND a referral of business to (or influence over the selection of) that provider
choice_b: A written contract between two licensees and a shared office location
choice_c: Common ownership of more than fifty percent and a shared marketing budget
choice_d: A referral of business only, regardless of any ownership or affiliate relationship
explanation: 12-10-218(1)(a) requires both (I) an affiliate relationship or a direct beneficial ownership interest of more than one percent in another settlement service provider, and (II) a referral of business to, or affirmative influence over the selection of, that provider.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under 12-10-218(1)(b), which of the following specifically qualifies a person as an "associate" of a person in a position to refer settlement service business?
choice_a: Any licensed real estate broker in Colorado, regardless of relationship
choice_b: A broker acting as an independent contractor for the person in a position to refer business
choice_c: A licensee's past client from an unrelated, closed transaction
choice_d: Any member of the same local real estate board
explanation: 12-10-218(1)(b)(III) defines an associate to include an employer, officer, director, partner, franchiser, or franchisee of the person, "including a broker acting as an independent contractor."

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a "settlement service" under 12-10-218(1)(c)?
choice_a: Property management services
choice_b: Home staging services
choice_c: Pest and fungus inspections
choice_d: Moving and relocation services
explanation: 12-10-218(1)(c)(XII) lists "pest and fungus inspections" among the enumerated settlement services; property management, home staging, and moving/relocation services do not appear anywhere in that list.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: A broker refers a buyer to an affiliated title company in which the broker holds an ownership interest. Under 12-10-218(2)(a), this affiliated business arrangement is permitted only if:
choice_a: The broker discloses the arrangement verbally at closing
choice_b: The buyer signs a waiver of any RESPA disclosure
choice_c: The commission pre-approves the specific transaction
choice_d: The broker's payment is only in the form of a return on investment, and the arrangement does not violate section 12-10-217
explanation: 12-10-218(2)(a) states an affiliated business arrangement is permitted where the person referring business receives payment only in the form of a return on an investment and where it does not violate section 12-10-217.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under 12-10-218(2)(b), when must a licensee who is part of an affiliated business arrangement disclose that arrangement to the parties in a real estate transaction?
choice_a: When an offer to purchase real property is fully executed
choice_b: Within 10 days after the listing agreement is signed
choice_c: Only at closing, and only if asked
choice_d: Within 30 days after the transaction closes
explanation: 12-10-218(2)(b) requires disclosure to all parties to the transaction when an offer to purchase real property is fully executed, and the disclosure must be written, signed by all parties, and comply with RESPA.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: A licensee tells a prospective buyer, "I will only represent you if you agree to use my affiliated home inspection company." Under 12-10-218(2)(c), this is:
choice_a: Permitted because the licensee has disclosed the affiliation
choice_b: Prohibited -- a licensee may not require the use of an affiliated business arrangement as a condition of obtaining the licensee's services
choice_c: Permitted only in commercial real estate transactions
choice_d: Permitted if the buyer initials a waiver form
explanation: 12-10-218(2)(c) prohibits a licensee from requiring the use of an affiliated business arrangement or a particular settlement service provider as a condition of obtaining that licensee's services.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: 12-10-218(2)(d) prohibits a licensee from doing which of the following?
choice_a: Disclosing an affiliated business arrangement to a client
choice_b: Referring a client to any settlement service provider
choice_c: Giving or accepting a fee, kickback, or other thing of value pursuant to an agreement or understanding that business will be referred to a provider of settlement services
choice_d: Charging a commission on a real estate sale
explanation: 12-10-218(2)(d) bars a licensee from giving or accepting any fee, kickback, or other thing of value pursuant to any agreement or understanding, oral or otherwise, that settlement-service business will be referred to a provider.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under 12-10-218(2)(e), payment of a fee is NOT prohibited when it is paid to:
choice_a: Any licensee who merely refers a client's name to an affiliated company
choice_b: A licensee's spouse regardless of services performed
choice_c: A settlement service provider simply for accepting a referral
choice_d: An attorney for services actually rendered
explanation: 12-10-218(2)(e)(I) specifically states nothing in the section prohibits payment of a fee to an attorney for services actually rendered.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under 12-10-218(2)(f)(II), which payment between real estate brokers is expressly not prohibited?
choice_a: A flat monthly stipend paid in exchange for exclusive referrals
choice_b: A percentage ownership transfer given in exchange for referrals
choice_c: A cash bonus for closing volume with no underlying agreement
choice_d: A fee paid pursuant to cooperative brokerage and referral arrangements or agreements between real estate brokers
explanation: 12-10-218(2)(f)(II) states nothing in the section prohibits payment of a fee pursuant to cooperative brokerage and referral arrangements or agreements between real estate brokers.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: An attorney represents a buyer in a real estate transaction and also issues the buyer's title insurance policy through a separate corporate title agency the attorney established as an adjunct to the law practice. Under 12-10-218(2)(g)(II), this arrangement:
choice_a: Automatically violates the anti-kickback provisions of the statute
choice_b: Is not a violation of this section
choice_c: Is allowed only with prior written commission approval
choice_d: Requires the client to use a different, unaffiliated title company
explanation: 12-10-218(2)(g)(II) states it is not a violation of the section for an attorney or law firm representing a client to issue or arrange for title insurance directly as agent or through a separate corporate title insurance agency the attorney or law firm established as an adjunct to its law practice.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under 12-10-218(2)(h), a person can avoid liability for a violation of the affiliated-business-arrangement statute by proving, by a preponderance of the evidence, that:
choice_a: The other party to the transaction consented in writing
choice_b: No consumer was financially harmed by the arrangement
choice_c: The violation was not intentional and resulted from a bona fide error, notwithstanding maintenance of procedures reasonably adopted to avoid the error
choice_d: The licensee was unaware that the statute existed
explanation: 12-10-218(2)(h) provides a bona fide error defense: no person is liable if they prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the violation was not intentional and resulted from a bona fide error despite reasonably adopted procedures to avoid it.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: How do the affiliated-business-arrangement disclosure obligations differ between an individual licensee and that licensee's employing broker under 12-10-218(3) and (4)?
choice_a: The licensee discloses only at initial licensure, and the employing broker never has to disclose
choice_b: Only the employing broker has any disclosure obligation
choice_c: The licensee must disclose annually, and the employing broker discloses only once, when first joining an arrangement
choice_d: The licensee discloses at the time of entering into or changing an arrangement, while the employing broker must disclose the names of all such arrangements at least annually
explanation: Under 12-10-218(3), a licensee discloses at the time the licensee enters into or changes an affiliated business arrangement, while under (4) the employing broker must, at least annually, disclose the names and physical locations of all affiliated business arrangements to which the broker is a party.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Per 12-10-218(5), rules the commission adopts concerning affiliated business arrangements must:
choice_a: Be less stringent than the federal HUD rules to ease compliance burden on licensees
choice_b: Be at least as stringent as the federal rules and ensure that consumers are adequately informed about affiliated business arrangements
choice_c: Apply only to commercial, not residential, real estate transactions
choice_d: Be approved by the insurance commissioner before taking effect
explanation: 12-10-218(5) requires that rules adopted by the commission be at least as stringent as the federal RESPA rules and ensure consumers are adequately informed; the commission consults with the insurance commissioner but neither may impose a conflicting regulatory burden.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under 12-10-219(1), disciplinary and license-denial proceedings before the commission are conducted by:
choice_a: The commission's executive director acting alone
choice_b: A three-member panel of active licensees
choice_c: An administrative law judge, pursuant to sections 24-4-104 and 24-4-105
choice_d: The county district attorney's office
explanation: 12-10-219(1) provides that, except as otherwise provided, all proceedings before the commission on disciplinary actions and denial of licensure shall be conducted by an administrative law judge under sections 24-4-104 and 24-4-105.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: If the licensee facing a disciplinary hearing is an employed broker, what does 12-10-219(2) require the commission to do?
choice_a: Automatically place the employing broker's own license on probation
choice_b: Notify the employing broker by first-class mail at the broker's last-known business address
choice_c: Require the employing broker to co-sign the hearing notice
choice_d: Move the hearing to the employing broker's county of residence
explanation: 12-10-219(2) requires the commission to notify the broker employing the licensee, by first-class mail, of a copy of the written notice required under section 24-4-104(3), sent to the employing broker's last-known business address.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under 12-10-219(3), what must occur before a license can be denied, suspended, or revoked?
choice_a: The commission must have made its decision by a majority vote
choice_b: The administrative law judge must personally issue the revocation order
choice_c: The licensee must have exhausted all appeals
choice_d: Two administrative law judges must independently concur
explanation: 12-10-219(3) states that no license shall be denied, suspended, or revoked until the commission has made its decision by a majority vote.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: In a hearing where a license could be denied, suspended, or revoked because of a felony conviction or a crime involving moral turpitude, 12-10-219(6) states the commission is governed by:
choice_a: Section 12-10-217
choice_b: Rule 9.7 of 4 CCR 725-1
choice_c: The federal Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act
choice_d: Section 24-5-101
explanation: 12-10-219(6) provides that in any hearing where license denial, suspension, or revocation is possible due to a felony conviction or a crime of moral turpitude, the commission is governed by section 24-5-101.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Comparing Rule 8.5 and Rule 8.7 of 4 CCR 725-1 Chapter 8, what distinction do they draw regarding judicial review of the commission's actions on a declaratory-order petition?
choice_a: Both a decision not to rule and an issued declaratory order are final agency actions subject to judicial review
choice_b: Neither a decision not to rule nor an issued declaratory order is subject to judicial review
choice_c: A decision not to rule on a petition is not final agency action subject to judicial review, but a declaratory order the commission actually issues does constitute agency action subject to judicial review
choice_d: Only a decision not to rule on the petition is subject to judicial review
explanation: Rule 8.5 states a decision not to rule on a petition for a declaratory order is not final agency action subject to judicial review, while Rule 8.7 states that a declaratory order issued on a petition constitutes agency action subject to judicial review under section 24-4-106, C.R.S.

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under Rule 9.4.B of 4 CCR 725-1 Chapter 9, if neither party files exceptions to an administrative law judge's initial decision, what happens?
choice_a: The commission must automatically schedule a new hearing
choice_b: The initial decision becomes the final order of the commission 30 days after the Division mails it to the parties
choice_c: The initial decision is void and the case must be refiled
choice_d: The parties retain an unlimited amount of time to later request review
explanation: Rule 9.4.B provides that if neither party appeals by filing exceptions, the initial decision becomes the final order of the commission 30 days after the Division mails the initial decision, and failure to file exceptions waives the right to judicial review of the final order (with a narrow exception).

topic: Affiliated Business Arrangements and Disciplinary Hearing Procedure
question: Under Rule 9.6 of 4 CCR 725-1 Chapter 9, if the commission grants a party's request for oral argument on exceptions, how much time does each party receive?
choice_a: Ten minutes to present their argument, not counting time used by the commission's questioning
choice_b: Thirty minutes, inclusive of any questioning by the commission
choice_c: Five minutes, with no extensions permitted under any circumstances
choice_d: As much time as the party deems necessary
explanation: Rule 9.6.B provides that if oral argument is granted, each party has ten minutes to present their argument, and questioning by commission members does not count against that allocated time.
